projects.name: DevFlow-AI
projects.tagline: AI code review, auto-fix & CI/CD — on your own servers
projects.overview: DevFlow-AI is a self-hosted platform that reviews pull requests with AI, proposes and applies fixes, and runs CI/CD for GitHub and GitLab — while guaranteeing the AI never changes a repository without permission.
projects.problem: Code review is slow and inconsistent, and most AI review tools either send your code to a third-party cloud or are allowed to push changes by themselves. Teams that care about privacy and control end up choosing between speed and safety.
projects.why: DevFlow-AI runs on your own infrastructure, works with free models (with a fully local fallback), and puts every write behind an approval rules engine. Teams get fast, consistent reviews without giving up control of their code — or their budget.
projects.audience: Engineering teams on GitHub or GitLab who want AI help in code review but must keep code private and changes controlled.
capabilities: Get an automatic AI review on every pull / merge request — summary, risks and line-level comments.
Ask specialised reviewers (code quality, security, analyst) for focused feedback.
Let the fixer agent propose a patch, then approve, reject or ask for changes before anything is written.
Run CI/CD pipelines and watch them live on a pipeline graph.
Control cost and privacy: route across 90 free models from 10 providers, or stay fully local with Ollama.
See AI usage, approvals and traces in a web console and Grafana dashboards with alerts.
built: 132 API endpoints, 31 database tables, 30 Celery background tasks and 17 Docker services.

A framework-free tool-calling agent loop for 9 roles (analyst, fixer, code reviewer, security reviewer…) with JSON-schema-validated output, token budgets and AST checks that suggested code still fits its callers.
An LLM router across 90 free models from 10 providers, with automatic cool-downs on rate limits and a local Ollama fallback.
An MCP gateway that sends every GitHub / GitLab write through 57 allow-listed tools, one-time keys and a deny-by-default go / ask / stop rules engine.
No-network, read-only Docker sandboxes for every review run.
A Next.js 16 / React 19 / Tailwind console with live pipeline graphs, approvals and AI usage.
OpenTelemetry tracing for FastAPI, Celery, SQLAlchemy and httpx into Grafana — 2 dashboards and 8 alert rules as code.
392 unit tests, 67 API end-to-end tests and 43 Playwright tests running in GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.

challenges.q: How do you stop an AI from changing code on its own?
challenges.a: Every write is a tool call through one MCP gateway — 57 allow-listed tools, one-time keys and a deny-by-default go / ask / stop rules engine.

challenges.q: Free models hit rate limits constantly.
challenges.a: The router spreads work across 90 models from 10 providers, cools down any that return rate-limit errors, and falls back to local Ollama.

challenges.q: How do you trust AI-written code?
challenges.a: Output is validated against JSON schemas, kept inside token budgets, and checked with AST analysis so a change still fits its callers.

projects.name: EU VAT Registration Platform
projects.tagline: Sole backend developer · live in production
projects.overview: A staff workspace and client portal that runs EU VAT registrations for overseas businesses — onboarding, documents, e-signatures and country-specific filing steps. I am the sole backend developer.
projects.problem: Registering for VAT across EU countries means a different process, document set and rule set for every country. Tracking that through emails and spreadsheets is slow, error-prone and hard to audit.
projects.why: Each country’s process lives in a versioned workflow engine, so new rules ship as data, every action is audited, and staff and clients always see exactly what they can do next — with security strong enough to pass three independent audits.
projects.audience: Overseas businesses registering for EU VAT, and the operations team that manages their filings.
capabilities: Clients onboard, upload documents and e-sign forms in a secure portal.
Staff move each registration through country-specific workflow steps.
Every user only sees the actions their role allows (4 roles, 21 permissions).
Documents are virus-scanned, encrypted and stored in Azure.
Automatic emails and 15 scheduled background jobs keep cases moving.
Every change is recorded in an append-only audit log.
built: 244 REST endpoints across 34 NestJS modules and 63 database models (PostgreSQL 17 + Prisma 7).
A data-driven workflow engine that runs each country’s registration process as versioned data — the same rules decide which actions each user can take.
Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC) sign-in, Postgres-backed sessions with CSRF protection, and role-based access with 4 roles and 21 permissions.
Azure Blob Storage, Azure Key Vault (AES-256-GCM for stored credentials), ClamAV / Defender virus scanning, Microsoft Graph email and Adobe Acrobat Sign — each behind a clean adapter.
A background worker on a Postgres transactional outbox that runs 15 scheduled jobs without Redis or a separate queue.
An append-only audit log written in the same transaction as every change, optimistic locking (ETag / If-Match), idempotency keys and RFC 9457 error responses.
A published OpenAPI contract the React team uses to generate typed API clients.
Passed 3 rounds of external security testing (VAPT); 63 Jest test files and a 24-suite end-to-end API harness.

challenges.q: Every country has a different process.
challenges.a: The workflow engine runs each country’s process as versioned data, so rules change without code changes — and the same rules drive permissions.

challenges.q: No double submissions, no lost updates.
challenges.a: Idempotency keys, optimistic locking with ETag / If-Match, and standard RFC 9457 error responses.

challenges.q: Reliable background jobs without extra infrastructure.
challenges.a: A Postgres transactional outbox runs 15 scheduled jobs — no Redis or separate queue needed.

projects.name: Hopline
projects.overview: Hopline sends files directly between devices — browser, desktop and command line — encrypted end to end, with no upload server holding your data.
projects.problem: Most file-sharing tools upload your file to someone’s cloud first. That is slower, size-limited, and someone else keeps a copy.
projects.why: Direct peer-to-peer transfer is faster, has no storage limit and keeps files private. Hopline makes it work across browsers, desktops and terminals, with resume and integrity checks built in.
projects.audience: Anyone moving big or private files — and developers who want to script transfers from the terminal.
capabilities: Send a file from browser to browser using a short pairing code.
Use the desktop app on Windows, macOS or Linux.
Script transfers from the command line.
Resume after a dropped connection — every chunk is verified with SHA-256.
Move huge files fast: 10 GiB in 56.8 seconds over encrypted TCP.
built: A Node.js WebSocket signaling server and a WebRTC protocol sending 64 KiB frames over up to 4 parallel connections, with flow control, SHA-256 verification and resume after a disconnect.
Encrypted TCP transfer for the CLI and desktop app (CPace PAKE key exchange, HKDF, AES-256-GCM): 10 GiB sent in 56.8 seconds with SHA-256 verification.
An Electron desktop app and a React 19 + Vite web app.
A hardened signaling server and TURN relay with rate limits and brute-force throttling.
90 automated tests, 4 rounds of security testing with every finding fixed, and a release pipeline that builds installers for 3 operating systems.

challenges.q: Fast without a server in the middle.
challenges.a: Parallel WebRTC channels with flow control, and encrypted TCP for CLI / desktop: 10 GiB in 56.8 seconds.

challenges.q: Pairing securely with a short code.
challenges.a: CPace PAKE turns a short code into a strong shared key, so the code can’t be brute-forced offline.

challenges.q: Abuse of a public signaling server.
challenges.a: Rate limits and brute-force throttling on signaling and TURN; 4 rounds of security testing with every finding fixed.
